summary: We developed an interactive educational mini-game designed to train "junior astronauts" in the fundamentals of space missions. The project addresses the challenge of making aerospace education engaging, accessible, and fun for younger generations. By combining gamified physics challenges with basic problem-solving tasks—such as managing oxygen levels, navigating through gravity shifts, and handling system alerts—players experience real-world scenarios astronauts face. This project is important because inspiring kids early through interactive tech builds the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers, sparking curiosity about Earth and space sciences in an immersive way
details: Our project is a browser/desktop-based mini-game where users step into the boots of a trainee astronaut. The gameplay involves interactive modules simulating microgravity movement, capsule maintenance, and quick decision-making during simulated space anomalies. It runs on clean game loops that test reflexes and basic logic t simplifies complex space concepts into an entertaining experience. The impact is sparking early interest in STEM fields, improving cognitive problem-solving under pressure, and educating kids about space exploration challenges in a playful environment. We built this using C++ / Python for backend logic and core mechanics, alongside web tools for the interface.
